title: U.S. House · California's 5th District
area: Covers part of the Sierra Nevada, including areas around Amador County, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, Tom McClintock (R) placed first with 61.3% (129,653 votes) and Michael Masuda (D) placed second with 24.3% (51,418 votes) out of 211,542 total votes cast; both advanced to the general election.

candidates.name: Tom McClintock
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 top-two primary with a majority of votes cast
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2023, prior district); Chair, Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement

summary.text: Tom McClintock has represented Sierra Nevada-area districts in the U.S. House since first winning election, previously working as a journalist and public policy analyst. He chairs the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement.

background.text: Born in 1956 in Bronxville, New York; earned a bachelor's degree in political science from UCLA in 1978.
Worked previously as a journalist and public policy analyst.
Has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey.

record.text: Chairs the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement for the 2025-2026 session.
Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources' Federal Lands and Water, Wildlife and Fisheries subcommittees, and on the House Committee on the Budget, for the 2025-2026 session.

candidates.name: Michael Masuda
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: Engineer; former U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Officer

summary.text: Michael Masuda is an engineer and former U.S. Department of State Foreign Affairs Officer who grew up in Amador County. He is the grandson of Japanese Americans who were forcibly interned during World War II and describes himself as a first-time candidate running to serve his home district.

background.text: Grew up in a town of about 200 people in Amador County; graduated from Amador High School and earned a graduate degree from California Polytechnic State University, San Luis Obispo, in 2013.
Worked as an engineer designing tools for the U.S. military, and later at the U.S. Department of State using his science and engineering background on foreign policy and national security matters.
Grandson of Japanese Americans from the Bay Area who were forcibly relocated and interned during World War II, and of German and Polish American farmers from Wisconsin.

priorities.text: Describes himself as an engineer rather than a politician, focused on effective solutions for the diverse valley, foothill, mountain, and desert communities of the district.
priorities.quote: I am an engineer, not a politician. I am focused on addressing our shared challenges and building a future for everyone to prosper.

researchNotes: Tom McClintock has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his official House website lists issue categories (e.g., California Water Crisis, Fiscal and Economic, Illegal Immigration) without accessible position statements, so no specific 2026 positions could be documented from it. Masuda has not held prior public office.
